image_description: A side-profile view of a bison standing on a grassy, dirt-covered slope. The bison is facing right, displaying its characteristic shoulder hump, shaggy dark brown fur on the forequarters, and a visible horn. The background consists of green vegetation and trees.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile. One horn is distinctly visible, appearing short and curved relative to the head size. The head structure appears broad and massive.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct cluster of long, dark hair hangs from the chin and throat area, matching the description of a beard.
The eye is visible as a dark spot on the side of the head, consistent with the description.
No prominent ears are sticking out; the ear region is covered by the thick fur of the head, consistent with 'hidden in fur'.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal exhibits a massive build with a significant height at the shoulders (withers), creating a sloping back towards the rear.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The forequarters are covered in thick, shaggy dark brown fur, and there is a very pronounced hump at the shoulder region.
The image is cropped such that the hindquarters and rear legs are largely outside the frame or obscured by the angle/crop. Only the front half to two-thirds of the body is clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible horn is relatively small compared to the massive size of the head and body.
The legs are cut off at the bottom of the frame before the hooves are visible. Therefore, cloven hooves cannot be verified.
The rear of the animal, including the tail, is outside the frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out look-alikes like cattle or yak.
To verify the structural integrity of the visible limbs and shoulder connection, ensuring no fusion or extra limbs.
To check for subtle texture anomalies in the fur and potential blending issues with the background vegetation.
To ensure sharp boundaries between the shaggy fur and the background, checking for edge bleeding.

focus_areas: Edge definition between subject and background
Anatomical correctness of the shoulder hump

Check if the eye has a realistic reflection/depth.
